articles.description:
Threads in Languages like c++ and JAVA


In the above mentioned languages, threads are a means of concurrency that takes a lot of cpu time in context switching and takes a relatively huge memory at the time of their creation. A single thread takes ~ 1 MB. Therefore, if you were to spawn 100,000 threads, you would need about 100 GB of RAM, which is not economically feasible for most of software projects. Also for maintaining concurrency, CPU generally uses timeslicing, to give equal number of cpu cycle to each thread. But while doing this, the CPU have to perform context switching. This whole thing is quite expensive, in terms of time because of saving current thread details in TCB(Process Control Block), loading the new thread TCB in memory and context switches destroy cache locality, caus…
